t:
The destruction wreaked by the floods in north India in August has evoked concern at the highest levels. Last month, a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud had suggested that an expert committee conduct a “complete and comprehensive” study on the carrying capacity of the Himalayan region. Following this, the Centre has proposed setting up a 13-member technical committee. “Carrying capacity” is a concept derived from population-biology and generally refers to the quantity of a species that can thrive sustainably in a defined ecosystem. Generally, population exceeding capacity will lead to a natural decline in numbers, as witnessed when grasslands or overgrazed or invasive species throttle existing biome. Applying these ideas in the context of hill-stations and Himalayan States — the challenge is between balancing rising population, infrastructural needs and the precarious geography — is bound to be a challenging enterprise. Going by recent history, it is unlikely that a disinterested scientific opinion will be palatable to every stakeholder in the Himalayan States. Following the devastating floods in Uttarakhand in 2013, the Supreme Court had appointed a committee of experts to evaluate the role of hydropower projects in the State. While the committee’s reports did influence a reduction in the proposed hydro projects, they failed to restrict road-widening projects and the carving up of mountainsides in ways that were deemed unsuitable for the topography.
The latest proposal by the Centre is not new; as far back as 2020, it had circulated, among the 13 Himalayan States, guidelines to assess the carrying capacity of their hill stations, cities and eco-sensitive zones. The Environment Ministry had in May reminded all the States to undertake such a study and submit them “as early as possible”. The crisis of land subsidence experienced in Joshimath, Uttarakhand, in January had also sparked a debate on the conflict between infrastructural development and ecology, but in a matter of months, Himachal Pradesh saw an unexpected deluge washing away roads and highways built on denuding mountains. More committees and reports will not change the reality that infrastructure development in the hills cannot be executed as in the plains. Either States must bear the higher cost that comes from building more sustainably and minimising the risk to denizens, or designate regions as no-go zones. The latter has for decades provided fertile ground for political opportunism. As unequivocal scientific evidence concludes, the option to kick the proverbial can down the road no longer exists. 
 Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the response of Himalayan States to the Centre's proposal in 2020?
o: They swiftly implemented the guidelines provided by the Centre.
They actively rejected the proposal due to its infeasibility.
They have been slow in conducting and submitting the necessary studies.
They promptly submitted detailed assessments for all their hill stations and eco-sensitive zones.
e:
C) They have been slow in conducting and submitting the necessary studies. 
 The passage mentions that "as far back as 2020, it had circulated, among the 13 Himalayan States, guidelines to assess the carrying capacity of their hill stations, cities and eco-sensitive zones." Later, it's stated that "The Environment Ministry had in May reminded all the States to undertake such a study and submit them 'as early as possible'." This indicates that the states had not yet submitted the studies by May, implying that they were slow in response.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. 
 Though the speaker used flowery expressions to convince the audience, they were intelligent enough to find out his ulterior intentions
o: to read between the lines
to be under somebody’s thumb
to cast pearls before swine
to not judge a book by its cover
e:
A)To read between the lines– To understand hidden or underlying meanings (छिपे हुए या अंतर्निहित अर्थ को समझना) 
 To be under somebody’s thumb(idiom) – To be under someone’s control. किसी के नियंत्रण में होना 
 To cast pearls before swine(idiom) – To offer something valuable to someone who does not appreciate it. अनमोल वस्तु को उसके महत्व को न समझने वाले को देना 
 To not judge a book by its cover(idiom) – To not form opinions based on outward appearances. बाहरी दिखावे के आधार पर राय न बनाना

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation. At the start of the workshop, the participants sat in silence, each feeling a bit nervous about meeting new colleagues. Sensing the tension, the facilitator decided to initiate a fun activity. She asked everyone to share an interesting fact about themselves. As people began to open up and share stories, laughter filled the room, and the atmosphere became more relaxed. What did the facilitator do?
o: Break the ice
Break a leg
Beat around the bush
Burn the midnight oil
e:
The participants were feeling nervous and tense at the beginning of the workshop. The facilitator sensed this tension and decided to initiate a fun activity by asking everyone to share an interesting fact about themselves. This helped to create a more relaxed and friendly atmosphere, encouraging people to open up and interact with each other. "Breaking the ice" means to initiate a conversation or activity to make people feel more comfortable in a social setting, especially when they are meeting each other for the first time. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. 
Break a leg: This is a phrase used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance or event.
Beat around the bush: Refers to avoiding the main topic or issue; speaking indirectly or evasively instead of addressing something directly.
Burn the midnight oil: To work late into the night; putting in extra effort or working hard, especially during late hours.

t: In the following question, a sentence is given with a phrase highlighted in bold. Select the option given below that can replace the phrase in bold to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct and mark that as your answer. If the sentence is correct as it is, mark 'No correction required', as the answer. The secretary and candidate have arrived at the office to give his nomination.
o: have been arrived
No correction required
were arrived
has arrived
e: A singular verb should be used when two singular nouns joined by 'and' refer to the same person or thing and only the first noun is denoted by an article. Therefore, in this sentence, the verb should be singular. So, the phrase 'have arrived' should be replaced with the phrase 'has arrived' to rectify the given sentence. The correct sentence is: The secretary and candidate has arrived at the office to give his nomination Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
After reviewing the proposal, the board of directors decided to <u>show approval</u> to the new marketing campaign.
o: Throw hat in the ring
Play with fire
Beat the dead horse
Give the green light
e:
Throw hat in the ring - To enter a competition or join an activity.
Play with fire - To engage in a risky or dangerous activity.
Beat the dead horse - To waste time on a futile issue or effort.
Give the green light - To give approval or permission for something to proceed.
Among the given options, the idiom 'give the green light' can accurately substitute the underlined segment.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

t: Select the most appropriate option that best expresses the meaning of the proverb in the given sentence. It's frustrating when people stick their oars in without understanding the full context of the situation.
o: To jump to conclusions
To behave rudely
To give an opinion without being asked
To start arguing for no reason
e: The most appropriate option that best expresses the meaning of the given proverb/idiom is 'to give an opinion without being asked.' The expression "stick one's oar in" means to interfere or offer input into a situation without being invited. In the context of the sentence, it implies frustration when people involve themselves in a matter without fully grasping the circumstances. Option (c) accurately captures this meaning by suggesting that people are giving their opinions without being solicited. Other options do not give the accurate meaning of the idiom. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation.
He is busy every night working on his project. He draws diagrams, conducts experiments, and writes up his findings until late in the night. Despite feeling tired, he knows that staying up late now will help him succeed in the competition. So, with his desk lamp on, he continues to work hard, determined to impress the judges with his project. What is he doing?
o: Burning the midnight oil
Flying off the handle
Spending a night on the town
Throwing in the towel
e: The most appropriate idiom for the given situation is 'burning the midnight oil'. 'Burning the midnight oil' means working late into the night, especially to complete a task or project. In the given context, the individual is diligently working on his project late into the night, despite feeling tired, with the determination to succeed in the competition. This aligns perfectly with the meaning of "burning the midnight oil." Other idioms are not suitable for the given context. 'Flying off the handle' means losing one's temper suddenly or becoming very angry. 'Spending a night on the town' means going out and enjoying oneself socially for the evening. 'Throwing in the towel' means giving up or surrendering, especially in the face of adversity. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t: Modern societies often celebrate progress through visible indicators—economic growth, technological penetration, and expanding infrastructure—while quietly overlooking fractures that resist quantification. Social inequality, though frequently acknowledged in rhetoric, is often treated as an abstract concern rather than a lived reality. The persistence of unequal access to education, healthcare, and legal recourse reveals that disparity is not merely a residual flaw of development but, in many cases, its unintended companion. Progress, when unevenly distributed, can deepen the very divides it claims to bridge. Public discourse tends to individualize social failure. Poverty is reframed as lack of effort, marginalization as absence of adaptability, and exclusion as personal deficiency. Such narratives offer moral comfort to the privileged by converting structural disadvantage into personal responsibility. Over time, this framing dulls collective urgency. When inequality is perceived as self-inflicted, social empathy is replaced by conditional sympathy—extended only to those deemed “deserving.” Institutions, meanwhile, respond with procedural solutions that emphasize efficiency over equity. Welfare systems grow increasingly conditional, access mechanisms become more complex, and accountability is measured through compliance rather than outcome. While these approaches appear neutral, they disproportionately burden those already navigating scarcity. The result is a paradoxical system in which assistance exists formally but remains functionally inaccessible to many. The most corrosive consequence of persistent inequality is not material deprivation alone but the erosion of social trust. When large sections of society experience the state as distant or indifferent, civic engagement weakens and resentment quietly accumulates. Addressing social issues, therefore, requires more than policy expansion; it demands a recalibration of how societies assign blame, distribute dignity, and define progress itself. In the sentence “Such narratives offer moral comfort to the privileged by converting structural disadvantage into personal responsibility,” the phrase “by converting structural disadvantage into personal responsibility” functions as:
o:
A
 relative clause modifying “narratives”

A
 noun clause acting as the object of “offer”

An
 adverbial phrase explaining the manner of action

A
 participial phrase indicating time
e: The Correct Answer is - An adverbial phrase explaining the manner of action. Explanation: The phrase explains how moral comfort is offered—through the act of reframing disadvantage. It modifies the verb “offer” by describing the method or manner. WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG: A is incorrect because the phrase does not describe “narratives” directly. B is wrong since the object of “offer” is “moral comfort.” D is incorrect as the phrase does not indicate time.

t:
Complete the dialogue for Person B using the correct idiom.
Person A: I am so nervous. I don't think I should make the speech tomorrow.
Person B: No. You are just getting ______. You have prepared for this.
o: hot feet
cold feet
cold hand
cold foot
e: The context suggests Person A is nervous and considering backing out of the speech. The idiom "getting cold feet" means becoming nervous or hesitant about a planned action, fitting perfectly. Person B reassures A that their nervousness is just hesitation and they are prepared. "Hot feet" is not a standard idiom, "cold hand" relates to poor circulation or fear in a different context, and "cold foot" is incorrect. Thus, "cold feet" is the correct choice.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation. At the company's annual dinner party, Sonal approached Mukesh, hoping to engage in friendly conversation and mend their strained relationship after a recent disagreement at work. However, Mukesh's responses remained short and dismissive, and he quickly excused himself to join a different group of colleagues. Which of the following best describes Mukesh's behaviour towards Sarah?"
o: Giving the cold shoulder
Keeping one's chin up
Hitting the hay
In the same boat
e:
Sonal approached Mukesh at the dinner party, hoping to mend their strained relationship after a disagreement. However, Mukesh responded with short, dismissive replies and quickly left to join another group of colleagues. This behaviour indicates that Mukesh was intentionally ignoring or being unfriendly towards Sonal, which aligns with the idiom "giving the cold shoulder." It means intentionally ignoring someone or treating them in a cold or unfriendly manner. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. 
Keeping one's chin up: Remaining cheerful or optimistic in difficult situations; staying positive despite challenges.
Hitting the hay: Going to bed or going to sleep; it's an informal idiom for going to sleep.
In the same boat: Sharing a similar situation or circumstance with someone else; facing the same problems or challenges together.

t:
In the question below, a sentence is given with a blank. From the options below, choose the correct idiom that can fit in the blank to make the sentence grammatically and meaningfully correct.
The basic advice with investment in the market is don't _________________.
o: give up the day job
put all your eggs in one basket
To make a long story short
Take a grain of salt
e: The sentence talks about what not to do while investing in the market. 'Put all your eggs in one basket (which means to depend for your success on a single person or plan of action)' adds meaning to the sentence as the sentence now become 'basic advice with investment is to not depend on a single plan of action'. Don't give up the day job' means 'to tell someone that you do not think they are very good at something'; it is contextually incorrect though it fits grammatically. 'To make a long story short' means 'to provide just the basic facts rather than giving a lengthy explanation'; it's grammatically incorrect. In option d) the correct idiom is 'take it with a grain of salt' not 'take a grain of salt'; it will be contextually incorrect. Hence, the answer is option b).

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation. Alex diligently completed his homework assignments each night and reviewed his notes regularly. Meanwhile, his classmates often procrastinated, leaving their homework until the last minute and cramming for exams. As the semester progressed, Alex's hard work paid off as he consistently achieved top grades. Which of the following best describes Alex's attitude?
o: A penny saved is a penny earned.
Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.
Bite off more than one can chew.
The early bird catches the worm.
e:
Alex consistently completed his homework and reviewed his notes regularly, showing a proactive and disciplined approach to his studies. He didn't wait until the last minute to do his work, unlike his classmates who procrastinated. As a result, Alex consistently achieved top grades, demonstrating that his early and consistent efforts paid off. This aligns with the idiom "The early bird catches the worm," which means that those who act promptly or start early are more likely to succeed or gain an advantage. Hence, (d) is the correct answer. 
A penny saved is a penny earned: This means that saving money is just as valuable as earning money, emphasizing the importance of frugality and wise financial management.
Don't count your chickens before they are hatched: Advises against assuming success before it's certain or before all the necessary steps have been taken; warns against premature optimism.
Bite off more than one can chew: Refers to taking on more tasks or responsibilities than one can handle; attempting something that is too difficult or ambitious.

t:
In the following sentence, four words or phrases have been underlined. One of them is incorrect. Choose the INCORRECT word or phrase from the given options.
American <u>officials says</u> this is <u>due to a lack of</u> transparency <u>surrounding</u> the virus <u>in</u> China
o: in
due to a lack of
surrounding
officials says
e: The phrase in option (d) is incorrect. According to the subject-verb agreement rule, we cannot use the singular verb 'says' with the plural subject 'officials'. Therefore, 'says' should be replaced with 'say' [plural verb] to rectify the given sentence. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

t: Which of the following phrases given below the sentence should replace the phrase given in bold to make the sentence grammatically correct? Choose the best option among the four given alternatives that reflects the correct phrase to be used in the sentence. I had to use trials and errors to figure out how to fix my car.
o: Trial and error
Trials and error
Trial and errors
A trial and an error
e: There are several phrases in English where two or more nouns are used together as a single noun and treated as singular. For example, bread and butter, black and white etc. 'Trial and error' is one such phrase, which refers to a process of solving a problem through repeated attempts and mistakes. So, the phrase in bold needs to be replaced by 'trial and error'. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.
Everyone knew about his impending resignation, but it remained <u>the obvious unaddressed problem</u> during the entire meeting.
o: a fish out of water
the elephant in the room
a wolf in sheep's clothing
a storm in a teacup
e:
The phrase "the obvious unaddressed problem" refers to a significant issue that everyone is aware of but no one discusses, often due to discomfort or sensitivity.
The idiom "the elephant in the room" means an obvious major problem or controversial issue that is conspicuously present but avoided as a subject for discussion. This perfectly describes the situation with his unmentioned resignation.
Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.
a) a fish out of water - someone who is uncomfortable in a particular or unfamiliar situation. (Describes a person's feeling, not an unaddressed issue.)
c) a wolf in sheep's clothing - a dangerous person who pretends to be harmless. (Describes a deceptive person, not an undiscussed topic.)
d) a storm in a teacup - a lot of unnecessary anger and worry about a matter that is not important. (Suggests the issue is trivial, which is not implied here.)
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t: Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted non-finite phrase. The students gathered in the auditorium to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration.
o: Functioning as a noun
Functioning as an adjective
Functioning as an adverb
Functioning as a subject
e: Answer: C) Functioning as an adverb Explanation: An infinitive phrase can function as a noun, adjective, or adverb. The highlighted phrase: “to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration” modifies the verb “gathered” and tells the purpose of gathering. gathered why? → to attend the orientation program Therefore, the phrase functions as an adverb. Why other options are incorrect: A) A noun functions as subject/object/complement. B) An adjective modifies a noun/pronoun, but this phrase modifies the verb “gathered.” D) The subject of the sentence is “The students.”

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
After much persuasion, my little brother finally <u>spilled the beans</u> about who broke the expensive vase.
o: Disclosure
Concealment
Cleansing
Ignorance
e:
The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly. In the sentence, the little brother finally disclosed the secret about who broke the vase.
a) Disclosure - Correct, as it means the act of making new or secret information known.
b) Concealment - Opposite of the idiom's meaning; it means hiding something.
c) Cleansing - Not related to revealing information; it means making something clean.
d) Ignorance - Means lack of knowledge, which is not what the idiom implies.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
The intern attempted to <u>steal his colleague's thunder</u> by claiming credit for the successful project.
o: Detraction
Support
Criticism
Applause
e:
The idiom "steal someone's thunder" means to take credit for someone else's achievements or ideas, or to lessen the impact or importance of what someone else does or says. In the sentence, the intern is trying to take credit and diminish his colleague's achievement.
a) Detraction - Correct, as it means the act of diminishing the worth, reputation, or importance of someone or something.
b) Support - Opposite of the idiom's meaning; it means to help or encourage.
c) Criticism - While the act might be criticized, the idiom itself isn't about criticizing.
d) Applause - Opposite, as the act aims to take applause away from another.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
After his initial proposal was rejected, he went _______________ and came back with a much better plan. His persistence paid off.
o: back to the drawing board
off the beaten path
over the top
down to the wire
e: The sentence describes a situation where an initial attempt failed, requiring a complete restart or a new approach to planning. The idiom should convey this idea of starting again from the beginning. The missing phrase must idiomatically describe the act of starting a planning process all over again because a previous attempt failed. Option a) is correct. This idiom means to start planning something again from the beginning because a previous attempt was unsuccessful. This perfectly fits the context of revising a rejected proposal. Option b) means to a place that is not well-known or popular; unconventional. This refers to location or method, not necessarily restarting a plan. Option c) means excessive or exaggerated. This doesn't fit the context of improving a plan. Option d) means until the very last moment. This refers to timing, not the process of replanning. Complete sentence: After his initial proposal was rejected, he went back to the drawing board and came back with a much better plan. His persistence paid off. Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. 
 Unless sales improve next month, the company will be in a critical position in which failure seems imminent
o: a mare's nest
a damp squib
up against the wall
hitting the sack
e:
C)Up against the wall(idiom) – In a difficult or critical situation where failure seems imminent मुश्किल या नाजुक स्थिति 
 A mare's nest(idiom) – A situation of confusion or a complicated mess. उलझन भरी स्थिति 
 A damp squib(idiom) – Something that is disappointing or fails to meet expectations. निराशाजनक परिणाम 
 Hitting the sack(idiom) – Going to bed to sleep. सोने जाना

t: In the following question, a statement has been given with highlighted text. Select the option that can replace the text with the correct idiom or phrase. If you put all your efforts into doing it, you would finish the job in an hour.
o: Put your mind to it
Have something in mind
Have a mind like a steel trap
Prey on somebody's mind
e:
The phrase 'put your mind to it' means to put all of your attention and efforts into doing it. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. 
Have something in mind- to be thinking about something as a possibility. 
Have a mind like a steel trap- to be able to think very quickly, clearly and intelligently· 
Prey on somebody's mind- to worry about something for a long time.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Constantly <u>crying wolf</u> over small matters means nobody believes you in a genuine crisis later.
o: Complaint
Deception
Exaggeration
Apology
e:
The idiom "cry wolf" means to raise a false alarm or ask for help when you do not need it, with the result that people do not believe you when you are really in trouble. In the sentence, it warns against making false alarms.
a) Complaint - While it may involve complaining, the core meaning is about the false alarm.
b) Deception - Correct, as raising a false alarm is a form of misleading or deceiving others about the reality of a situation.
c) Exaggeration - Close, but "cry wolf" specifically refers to a false alarm leading to future disbelief, which is a form of deception.
d) Apology - Not related to the meaning of raising a false alarm.
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
Despite their different backgrounds, the two colleagues _______________ on most important issues. They worked well together.
o: saw eye to eye
turned a blind eye
pulled strings
kept their chins up
e: The sentence describes a situation where two colleagues, despite differences, agree on important matters, leading to good teamwork. The idiom should express this agreement or shared perspective. The missing phrase must idiomatically convey the idea of being in agreement or having the same opinion as someone else. Option a) is correct. This idiom means to agree with someone or have the same opinion as them. This perfectly describes the colleagues' harmonious working relationship on key issues. Option b) means to pretend not to notice something, especially something wrong. This is unrelated to agreement. Option c) means to use one's influence, especially secretly, to get an advantage. This doesn't fit the context of agreement on issues. Option d) means to remain cheerful in a difficult situation. While positive, it doesn't specifically refer to agreement. Complete sentence: Despite their different backgrounds, the two colleagues saw eye to eye on most important issues. They worked well together. Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
In the following question, choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/ phrase underlined in the sentence.
I got out my wallet and began <u>to dole out</u> the money.
o: To be in low spirits.
To give out in small quantities.
To be faced with two dangerous situations.
To be in such a situation that it is difficult to decide what to do.
e:
'To dole out' means to give out in small quantities. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 
The figurative expression for 'to be in low spirits' is - To be in the doldrums. 
The figurative expression for 'to be faced with two dangerous situations' is - To be between the devil and the deep sea. 
The figurative expression for 'to be in such a situation that it is difficult to decide what to do' is - To be on the horns of a dilemma.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom (in the context) to fill in the sentence. 
 Making the final paper was a really difficult task but by the end of the week, I was able to_________
o: bark up the wrong tree
wrap my head around it
cry my eyes out
run out of steam
e: B) wrap my head around it'का इस्तेमाल किया जाएगा क्योंकि इसका अर्थ है किसी कठिन समस्या या विषय को समझना। वाक्य में बताया गया है कि अंतिम कागज बनाना कठिन था, परंतु सप्ताह के अंत तक, मैं इसे समझने में सक्षम था, इसलिए 'wrap my head around it' यहाँ सही है। जबकि 'A. bark up the wrong tree' का अर्थ है गलत जगह पर समस्या का हल ढूंढना, 'C. cry my eyes out' का अर्थ है बहुत रोना, और 'D. run out of steam' का अर्थ है ऊर्जा या उत्साह खो देना, जो इस context में सही नहीं है।

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment. 
 After years of heavy use, the old laptop began to stop functioning properly, no longer working well despite repeated repairs.
o: Double down on
let one’s guard down
Be no cakewalk
Grind to a halt
e:
D)Grind to a halt(phrase) – To gradually slow down and stop working or functioning. धीरे-धीरे बंद हो जाना 
 Double down on(idiom) – To strengthen one's commitment to a strategy or course of action. अपनी रणनीति पर डटे रहना 
 Let one’s guard down(idiom) – To relax and stop being careful or vigilant. सतर्कता छोड़ देना 
 Be no cakewalk(idiom) – To be difficult or challenging. आसान न होना

t: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'After the government interventions, the enrolment and retention of female students have increased by leaps and bounds.'
o: Slowly
Swiftly
Minimally
Gradually
e: 'By leaps and bounds' means making very rapid progress or growing very quickly, in a sudden and remarkable way. Among the options, swiftly best captures the idea of rapid growth. Note: While 'swiftly' is given as the correct option, 'rapidly' or 'dramatically' would be even more precise synonyms in normal usage. Origin: Believed to come from the sport of long jump, where athletes make a running start and leap as far as possible; first used in the 16th century for physical activity, later used metaphorically for rapid progress.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Despite his fear, the soldier had to <u>bite the bullet</u> and advance towards the enemy lines.
o: Retreat
Complaint
Endurance
Celebration
e:
The idiom "bite the bullet" means to face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage and stoicism. In the sentence, the soldier had to bravely endure the dangerous situation.
a) Retreat - Opposite of facing the situation courageously.
b) Complaint - The idiom implies acceptance without complaint, not voicing dissatisfaction.
c) Endurance - Correct, as it means the ability or strength to continue or last, especially despite fatigue, stress, or other adverse conditions.
d) Celebration - Not appropriate for a fearful or difficult situation.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Identify the idiom that conveys the meaning given in brackets.
The citizens were (angry and protesting strongly) after the controversial policy was announced by the government.
o: Up in arms
Up on the arm
Up on fire
Up the fire
e: The correct idiom for the given meaning is 'up in arms', as it effectively conveys the idea of being angry and protesting strongly. The idiom 'up in arms' means to be very angry and ready to fight or protest about something (angry and protesting strongly). The phrases in options (b), (c), and (d) are not standard English idioms and they do not convey the intended meaning. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom (in the context) to fill in the sentence. 
 Suman really has ______. She moved to a new house just a month back but already has a lovely garden
o: a heart of gold
bad hair day
a foot in the door
green fingers
e: D) Green fingers'का use होगा क्योंकि "green fingers" का अर्थ होता है बग़िचे को अच्छे से देखभाल करने की क्षमता। Sentence में mention किया गया है कि Suman ने एक महीने पहले ही नया घर खरीदा है लेकिन उसके पास पहले ही एक सुंदर बगिचा है, इसलिए 'green fingers' यहाँ सही है। जबकि 'a heart of gold' का अर्थ है बहुत अच्छा होना, 'bad hair day' का अर्थ है बुरा दिन होना, और 'a foot in the door' का अर्थ है किसी क्षेत्र में प्रवेश करना, जो इस context में सही नहीं है।

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
She had been working non-stop for a month, so her doctor advised her to _______________ for a week. Rest was essential.
o: paint the town red
hit the books
let her hair down
jump the gun
e: The sentence indicates that the person has been working very hard and needs to relax and take a break. The idiom should reflect this need for rest and unwinding. The missing phrase must idiomatically describe the act of relaxing and enjoying oneself after a period of hard work. Option c) is correct. This idiom means to relax and enjoy oneself, often after working hard or being under stress. This fits the doctor's advice for rest. Option a) means to go out and enjoy oneself flamboyantly, often by drinking and partying. While it involves enjoyment, it might not be the restful break the doctor advised. Option b) means to study hard. This is the opposite of what is needed. Option d) means to do or say something too soon, before the right time. This is irrelevant to taking a break. Complete sentence: She had been working non-stop for a month, so her doctor advised her to let her hair down for a week. Rest was essential. Hence, option (c) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom  to fill in the blank given the underlined segment in the following sentence 
 The Chancellor must ________________ about his plans for increasing taxation.
o: Cast a long shadow over
Lend an ear
Come clean
Find a middle ground
e:
C)Come clean about(phrase) – To confess or admit something openly and honestly. सच-सच कहना 
 Cast a long shadow over(idiom) – To have a negative influence that causes worry or sadness. प्रभाव डालना 
 Lend an ear(idiom) – To listen to someone sympathetically. ध्यान से सुनना 
 Find a middle ground(idiom) – To make a compromise between two opposing viewpoints. बीच का रास्ता निकालना

t:
Select the option that can substitute the underlined word in the given idiom. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'. 
A taste of your own <u>drink</u>.
o: Juice
No substitution required
Cooking
Medicine
e:
The given idiom is "A taste of your own drink." The underlined word here is "drink", which needs to be replaced by the word 'medicine'. 
The idiom "A taste of your own medicine" means experiencing the same harmful or unpleasant thing that one has been doing to others. It's a metaphorical way of saying that someone is being treated the way they have treated others.
Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence. The candidate blamed the persistent traffic jam as reason of his being late and the interviewer believed him though he was not convinced.
o: gave the benefit of doubt
changed his tune
thought err is human and to forgive is divine
did not judge the book by its cover
e: "Gave the benefit of doubt" (संदेह का लाभ देना) means to accept someone's statement as true despite some uncertainty about its accuracy, trusting their good intentions when there is ambiguity. "Changed his tune" means altering one's opinion; the other options describe forgiveness or not judging by appearance, which don't match this context.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence. He was alone and knew the dangers ahead during his journey, but he tried to keep up his confidence.
o: whistled in the dark
made of sterner stuff
stepped up his game
wouldn't be caught dead
e: "Whistled in the dark" (डर के बावजूद हिम्मत दिखाना) means trying to remain brave or pretending to be unafraid in a scary or uncertain situation. "Made of sterner stuff" describes inherent strength of character; "stepped up his game" means improving performance; "wouldn't be caught dead" expresses strong dislike — none precisely match "trying to keep up confidence."

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom  to fill in the blank given the underlined segment in the following sentence 
 The innocent bystanders were unfortunate enough to be ________________ during the heated argument between the two opposing groups.
o: Laid the stress
Plugged the gap
Gone a long way
Caught in the crossfire
e:
D) Caught in the crossfire– To be unintentionally harmed or involved in a conflict between two opposing parties. बीच में फंस जाना 
 Laid the stress– To emphasize something. जोर देना 
 Plugged the gap– To fill a deficiency or provide something that is missing. कमी पूरी करना 
 Gone a long way– To have made significant progress. बहुत आगे बढ़ जाना

t: Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase. Having completed the presentation successfully, the senior analyst submitted the final report to the management.
o: Infinitive Phrase
Gerund Phrase
Participial Phrase
Noun Phrase
e: Answer: C) Participial Phrase Explanation: A participial phrase begins with a participle and functions as an adjective. The highlighted phrase begins with: “Having completed” which is a participle form. The phrase describes the “senior analyst.” Which analyst? → analyst having completed the presentation successfully Therefore, it is a participial phrase. Why other options are incorrect: A) An infinitive phrase begins with “to + verb.” B) A gerund phrase functions as a noun. D) A noun phrase functions as a noun and does not begin with a participle.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom used in the given sentence. 
The coach hit the ceiling when he found out the team had skipped practice to go to a party.
o: Reached the rooftop
Severe punishment
Become angry
Ignore the situation
e: The most appropriate meaning of the idiom "hit the ceiling" is 'become angry'. The idiom "hit the ceiling" is used to describe a sudden outburst of anger or extreme frustration. In the sentence, it suggests that the coach became very angry upon discovering that the team had skipped practice to attend a party. Other options do not give the appropriate meaning of the idiom. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.
The student felt he <u>was rescued from the difficult situation by the final signal</u> as the exam ended.
o: saved by the bell
cost an arm and a leg
cut to the chase
fit as a fiddle
e:
The phrase "was rescued from the difficult situation by the final signal" means that an unwelcome or challenging situation was brought to an end by an external event, often at the last moment.
The idiom "saved by the bell" means to be rescued from a difficult or awkward situation at the very last moment, often by an interruption. This perfectly describes the student's relief at the exam ending.
Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.
b) cost an arm and a leg - to be extremely expensive. (Unrelated to being rescued from a situation.)
c) cut to the chase - to get to the main point quickly, avoiding unnecessary details. (Unrelated to being rescued.)
d) fit as a fiddle - to be in very good physical health. (Unrelated to the exam situation.)
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
The new intern was so nervous on his first day that he felt like _______________. He wasn't sure how to behave.
o: a bull in a China shop
a fish out of water
a wolf in sheep's clothing
a couch potato
e: The sentence describes an intern feeling nervous and unsure in a new environment. The idiom should express a feeling of being out of place or uncomfortable. The missing phrase must idiomatically convey the intern's discomfort and unfamiliarity with the situation. Option b) is correct. This idiom means to feel awkward or uncomfortable because you are in a situation that you are not used to. This perfectly describes the intern's feelings. Option a) means someone who is very clumsy and often breaks things in a delicate situation. While the intern is nervous, the sentence doesn't specifically imply clumsiness causing damage. Option c) means a dangerous person pretending to be harmless. This is entirely unrelated to an intern's nervousness. Option d) means a lazy person who spends a lot of time watching television. This has no connection to the intern's situation. Complete sentence: The new intern was so nervous on his first day that he felt like a fish out of water. He wasn't sure how to behave. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

t: Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase. The committee appointed a special team to investigate the financial irregularities reported during the audit.
o: Gerund Phrase
Participial Phrase
Noun Phrase
Infinitive Phrase
e: Answer: D) Infinitive Phrase Explanation: An infinitive phrase begins with “to + base verb” and may function as a noun, adjective, or adverb. The highlighted phrase begins with: “to investigate” Hence, it is an infinitive phrase. Here, it functions as an adjective because it describes the purpose of the “special team.” Which team? → team to investigate the financial irregularities Why other options are incorrect: A) A gerund phrase begins with an -ing form acting as a noun. B) A participial phrase begins with a participle (-ing/-ed form). C) A noun phrase functions purely as a noun and is not built around “to + verb.”

t: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute italicised words in the given sentence. The company denied spending on the pompous exhibitions for the clients.
o: Dog and pony show
Hold dear
Shoot for the moon
Cost an arm and a leg
e:
Dog and pony show: A presentation or performance that is overly elaborate or showy, often for promotional purposes.
Hold dear: To value or cherish something or someone greatly.
Shoot for the moon: To set ambitious or lofty goals; to aim for something very challenging.
Cost an arm and a leg: To be extremely expensive or costly.
Among the given options, the idiom 'dog and pony show' can correctly substitute the italicised words in the sentence.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. 
 This is going to be overwhelming for you as you have taken on work beyond your capabilities.
o: called it a day
at the eleventh hour
bitten off more than you can chew
put something on ice
e:
C) Bitten off more than you can chew(idiom)- taken on work beyond your capabilities (अपनी क्षमता से अधिक काम लेना)called it a day(idiom) – Stop working on something काम समाप्त करना 
 at the eleventh hour(idiom) – At the last possible moment अंतिम क्षण में 
 put something on ice(idiom) – Postpone or delay something किसी चीज़ को स्थगित करना या टालना

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. 
 Never believe anything you hear from others. Try to get every bit of information _____________, if possible.
o: in the fast lane
straight from the horse's mouth
down the line
fair and square
e:
B) straight from the horse's mouth' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है कि कोई जानकारी सीधा मूल स्रोत से प्राप्त की जा रही है। यहाँ पर जो संदेश दिया जा रहा है वह यह है कि आपको दूसरों से सुनी गई बात पर विश्वास नहीं करना चाहिए और यदि संभव हो, तो सीधा मूल स्रोत से जानकारी प्राप्त करनी चाहिए। इसलिए, 'straight from the horse's mouth' सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प होगा। 
 B)Straight from the horse's mouth(idiom) - directly from the original source; getting information directly from the most reliable source. सीधे स्रोत से

t: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute italicised words in the given sentence. The report's introduction provides a complete view of the new project.
o: Apple of the eye
Bird's eye view
One trick pony
Fish out of water
e:
Apple of the eye: Cherished above all others; a person's favourite.
Bird's eye view: An overall or panoramic view; a comprehensive perspective.
One trick pony: Someone or something with only one special talent or ability.
Fish out of water: A person who feels uncomfortable or out of place in a particular situation.
Among the given options, the idiom 'bird's eye view' can correctly substitute the italicised words in the sentence.
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom used in the given sentence. 
The argument over who forgot to refill the coffee machine was just a storm in a teacup.
o: A controversial issue that divided opinions
A significant achievement
Great outrage about a trivial matter
A calm and peaceful resolution
e: The most appropriate meaning of the idiom "a storm in a teacup" is 'great outrage about a trivial matter'. The idiom "a storm in a teacup" is used to describe a situation where there is a lot of fuss, commotion, or outrage over something that is relatively unimportant or insignificant. In the sentence, it suggests that the argument or dispute about who forgot to refill the coffee machine was blown out of proportion considering the trivial nature of the issue. Other options do not give the appropriate meaning of the idiom. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.
She accidentally <u>revealed the secret</u> about the surprise party when talking to the birthday boy.
o: hit the nail on the head
went down in flames
let the cat out of the bag
burned her bridges
e:
The phrase "revealed the secret" refers to disclosing information that was meant to be concealed, especially if done carelessly.
The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake. This perfectly fits the context of accidentally telling someone about a surprise party planned for them.
Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.
a) hit the nail on the head - to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem, or to say something that is exactly right. (Not about revealing a secret.)
b) went down in flames - to fail spectacularly. (Unrelated to revealing information, though revealing the secret might lead to the party "going down in flames" in terms of surprise.)
d) burned her bridges - to destroy one's path, connections, or opportunities, especially in a professional sense or a relationship. (Refers to ruining relationships, not just revealing a single secret.)
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom (in the context) to fill in the sentence. 
 Radha is unable to continue working in this office. Hard work is ______ on her health.
o: making her meet both ends
blowing hot and cold
keeping an eye
taking a toll on
e: D)Taking a toll on'का use होगा क्योंकि "taking a toll on" का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज को नकरात्मक प्रभाव पहुंचाना। Sentence में mention किया गया है कि Radha के स्वास्थ्य पर कठिन कार्य का बुरा प्रभाव पड़ रहा है, इसलिए 'taking a toll on' यहाँ सही है। जबकि 'making her meet both ends' का अर्थ होता है दोनों सिरों का मिलान, 'blowing hot and cold' का अर्थ है अनिश्चित विचार रखना, और 'keeping an eye' का अर्थ है ध्यान देना, जो इस context में सही नहीं है।

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill the blank in the given situation.
I thought Sadhna would always stick by me, but when I got into trouble, she turned out to be a/an ___________.
o: hard nut to crack
open secret
fair-weather friend
white elephant
e:
· Fair-weather friend - Someone who supports you only when things are good but leaves you in tough times.
· Hard nut to crack: A difficult problem or challenge to solve.
· Open secret: A secret that is widely known but not officially acknowledged.
· White elephant: A burdensome or costly possession, often difficult to dispose of.

t:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank.
If the allied forces of the rival countries want to vanquish the common enemy, they need to ____________ first.
o: stir the hornet's nest
keep the wolf from the door
live in a fool's paradise
mend their fences
e: Mend their fences: to make peace. It is in context to the fact that if hostile countries' allied armies seek to defeat a common enemy, they must first make peace. The rest of the idioms don't fit in the context of the sentence. Therefore, the correct answer is: (d) mend their fences. Additional Information: The meanings of the rest of the idioms are given below in the table:IdiomMeaningstir the hornet's nestraise controversykeep the wolf from the doorto avoid starvationlive in a fool's paradisefalse hope

t:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.
When listening to the politician's promises, it's wise to <u>regard them with some scepticism</u>.
o: go the extra mile
cry over spilt milk
take them with a grain of salt
bite off more than one can chew
e:
The phrase "regard them with some scepticism" refers to not fully believing something or being doubtful about its truth or likelihood. The idiom "take something with a grain of salt" means to not completely believe something that you are told because you think it is unlikely to be true or accurate. Here, "them" (implied "it" in the base idiom "take it with a grain of salt") refers to the promises. This fits the context of being cautious about a politician's promises. Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.
a) go the extra mile - to make a special effort. (Unrelated to skepticism.)
b) cry over spilt milk - to be unhappy about what cannot be undone. (Unrelated to believing promises.)
d) bite off more than one can chew - to take on a task that is too big or difficult. (Unrelated to scepticism about statements.)
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom that means the same as the given sentence. 
Just because the restaurant has a fancy exterior, it doesn't mean the food is good.
o: Don't cry over spilled milk.
Don't judge a book by its cover.
The early bird catches the worm.
Strike while the iron is hot.
e:
The sentence means that even though the restaurant looks impressive from the outside, it doesn't necessarily mean the food inside is of good quality. The idiom that best fits this situation is: Don't judge a book by its cover. This idiom means that you shouldn't form opinions about something or someone based solely on outward appearances because they may be misleading. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
Don't cry over spilled milk: This means not getting upset over something that has already happened and cannot be changed.
The early bird catches the worm: This means that being proactive and taking action early can lead to success or an advantage.
Strike while the iron is hot: This means to take advantage of an opportunity promptly, while conditions are favourable or circumstances are right.

t: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase. DRIVE SOMEONE UP THE WALL
o: To help someone achieve success
To overcome an obstacle by going over it
To close someone's path of escape
Make someone very irritated or angry
e: "Drive someone up the wall" is an informal idiom meaning to irritate, infuriate, or frustrate someone to an extreme degree. (Hindi: किसी को बहुत परेशान करना / चिड़चिड़ाहट पैदा करना) Example: His constant humming drives me up the wall. The imagery is of someone being so frustrated they could metaphorically "crawl up a wall." It has nothing to do with physical obstacles, helping someone, or blocking escape — those options are literal, incorrect interpretations.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
I don't know all the details yet; I've only heard it _______________. I need more concrete information.
o: through the grapevine
in a nutshell
from the horse's mouth
out of the blue
e: The sentence indicates that the speaker has received information informally or through rumours, not from an official source, and therefore lacks complete details. The idiom should reflect this informal way of hearing news. The missing phrase must idiomatically describe hearing information passed from person to person, often as rumour or gossip. Option a) is correct. This idiom means to hear news or information informally, through a network of personal contacts or rumours, rather than from an official source. This fits the context perfectly. Option b) means in a very brief way, using few words. While the information might be incomplete, this idiom refers to conciseness, not the source. Option c) means from the original or most reliable source. This is the opposite of what the sentence implies. Option d) means unexpectedly or without warning. This refers to the manner of occurrence, not the source of information. Complete sentence: I don't know all the details yet; I've only heard it through the grapevine. I need more concrete information. Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following statement. 
The intense argument between the two colleagues turned into a dramatic and spectacular session.
o: Steal someone's thunder
Blood and thunder
All wet
Off the hook
e:
The statement describes an intense argument between two colleagues that turned into a dramatic and spectacular session. The idiom "Blood and thunder" is a figurative expression that is often used to describe a situation or event characterized by intense emotions, conflict, and drama. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 
"Steal someone's thunder" means to take credit for someone else's achievements or to overshadow someone else's success. 
"All wet" is an informal expression meaning completely wrong or mistaken. 
"Off the hook" typically means being released from an obligation or responsibility.

t: Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase. Swimming regularly in cold water improved the athlete’s stamina and mental endurance significantly.
o: Participial Phrase
Infinitive Phrase
Gerund Phrase
Adjective Phrase
e: Answer: C) Gerund Phrase Explanation: A gerund phrase begins with a gerund (-ing form of a verb) and functions as a noun in a sentence. The highlighted phrase begins with: “Swimming” and the entire phrase acts as the subject of the verb “improved.” what improved the athlete’s stamina? → Swimming regularly in cold water Therefore, it is a gerund phrase. Why other options are incorrect: A) A participial phrase functions as an adjective, not as a noun. B) An infinitive phrase begins with “to + verb.” D) An adjective phrase modifies a noun or pronoun.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. 
 Bheem has been shown in the popular culture as someone who eats in large quantity.
o: eat humble pie
eat like a bird
eats like a horse
chews the fat
e:
C)Eats like a horse(idiom) – Someone who eats a lot; has a large appetite. भूख बहुत ज्यादा होना, बहुत अधिक खाना। 
 Eat humble pie(idiom): To admit one’s mistake and apologize; अपनी गलती मानकर माफी मांगना। 
 Eat like a bird(idiom): To eat very little; बहुत कम खाना। 
 Chews the fat(idiom): To have a casual, leisurely conversation; आराम से बातचीत करना।

t:
Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. 
 You must not participate in the marathon this year without any training. It is an unreal hope on your part!
o: carrying coal to new castle
a pipe dream
a will-o’-the-wisp
to lose one’s temper
e:
B)a pipe dream(idiom) – An unreal hope असत्य आशा 
 carry/take coals to Newcastle(phrase) – to supply something to a place or person that already has a lot of that particular thing 
 a will-o’-the-wisp(phrase) – something that is impossible to get or achieve 
 lose one’s temper(phrase) – to get angry अपना आपा खोना

t:
Identify the proverb that best suits the following scenario.
When too many people work together on a project as the lead, the final output is substandard.
o: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Actions speak louder than words.
A stitch in time saves nine.
Too many cooks spoil the broth.
e:
Among the given options, the proverb 'too many cooks spoil the broth' correctly represents the given scenario in the question, and it means 'if too many people are involved in a task or activity, especially as the lead, it will not be done well'.
Hence, (d) is the correct answer.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step: It is necessary to take the first step to achieve a long-term goal.
Actions speak louder than words: What people do is more significant than what they say.
A stitch in time saves nine: Address problems or challenges promptly to prevent them from becoming more significant and requiring more effort to fix.

t:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank.
Though Tom is super successful, no one genuinely looks up to him because he likes to ______________.
o: fish in troubled waters
fight to the finish
foot the bill
hang fire
e: Fish in troubled waters: to take advantage of the trouble of others. It is in context to the fact that even though Tom is extremely successful, no one truly respects him since he prefers to take advantage of the trouble of others. The rest of the idioms don't fit in the context of the sentence. Therefore, the correct answer is: (a) fish in troubled waters. Additional Information: The meanings of the rest of the idioms are given below in the table:IdiomMeaningfight to the finishFight till the endfoot the billbear expenseshang fireremain unsolved

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom (in the context) to fill in the sentence. 
 Pallavi worked really hard for the examination and ______ to gain success
o: struck a sour note
hit the bull’s eye
beat about the bush
left no stone unturned
e: D)Left no stone unturned'इधर use होगा क्योंकि इसका अर्थ है कि हर संभावित कोशिश की गई है। Sentence में mention किया गया है कि Pallavi ने परीक्षा के लिए कड़ी मेहनत की और सफलता पाने के लिए हर संभावना को देखा, इसलिए 'left no stone unturned' यहाँ सही है। जबकि 'Struck a sour note' का अर्थ है कुछ गलत कर देना, 'Hit the bull’s eye' का अर्थ है सही लक्ष्य पर पहुँचना, और 'Beat about the bush' का अर्थ है घुमाना फिराना, जो इस context में सही नहीं हैं।

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following statement.
He seems like he's just pretending to be threatening and isn't causing any real harm.
o: The ball is in your court.
All bark and no bite.
Don't bite the hand that feeds you.
Let sleeping dogs lie.
e:
"All bark and no bite" describes someone who makes a lot of noise or gives the appearance of being active or threatening, but in reality, they do nothing significant or don't follow through.
"The ball is in your court" means that it is now your responsibility to take action or make a decision.
"Don't bite the hand that feeds you" means that you shouldn't harm or be ungrateful toward someone who is helping or supporting you.
"Let sleeping dogs lie" means that it's best to avoid interfering with something that is currently at rest or causing no trouble.
Hence, option (b) is correct.

t: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom: 'Instead of confusing others, let us call a spade a spade in front of the audience.'
o: Pretend superiority
Remain silent
Speak truthfully
Be in conflict
e: 'Call a spade a spade' means to speak frankly and directly, without disguising or softening what one means; to say things as they really are - the idiom encourages direct, honest communication without euphemism or evasion. Pretend superiority is unrelated. Remain silent is the opposite of the idiom's meaning. Be in conflict is unrelated. Origin: The phrase dates back to ancient Greek texts and has been used in English since the 16th century to mean plain-speaking.

t: Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence. She is a highly respected cardiologist who specialises at the treatment of heart disease.
o: Specialise of
Specialises to
Specialises in
Specialises on
e:
The verb "specialises" is followed by the preposition "in" when indicating the area or field in which someone has expertise or focuses their professional work. Hence, (c) is the correct answer. 
The final sentence would be: She is a highly respected cardiologist who specialises in the treatment of heart disease.

t: Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence. The success of the project depends over your cooperation.
o: Depends off
Depends under
Depends on
Depends at
e:
Collocations are combinations of words that frequently occur together and have become established as natural expressions in a language. In this case, the verb "depend" is commonly used with the preposition "on" to indicate what something relies on. Hence, (c) is the correct answer. 
The final sentence would be: The success of the project depends on your cooperation.

t: Identify the type of the highlighted phrase. The committee discussed the rapid decline in employee productivity during the annual meeting.
o: Gerund Phrase
Adverb Phrase
Noun Phrase
Participial Phrase
e: Answer: C) Noun Phrase Explanation: A noun phrase is a group of words that functions as a noun in a sentence. The highlighted phrase: “the rapid decline in employee productivity” acts as the object of the verb “discussed.” discussed what? → the rapid decline in employee productivity Therefore, it is a noun phrase. Why other options are incorrect: A) A gerund phrase begins with an -ing verb functioning as a noun. B) An adverb phrase modifies a verb, adjective, or adverb. D) A participial phrase functions as an adjective and is built around a participle.

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 
 In light of his financial situation, he decided to cancel his holiday plans​​​​​
o: Appreciation of
Because of
Poor light to be replaced
A dark room
e:
B) 'In light of'एक अंग्रेजी मुहावरा है जिसका अर्थ होता है 'किसी विशेष स्थिति या जानकारी के आधार पर'। दिए गए वाक्य में, उसकी वित्तीय स्थिति के मद्देनजर, उसने अपनी छुट्टी की योजनाओं को रद्द करने का फैसला किया। इसलिए, यहां 'In light of' का अर्थ होगा 'Because of' (क्योंकि)। 
 'In light of' is an English idiom that means 'considering or based on a particular piece of information'. In the given sentence, considering his financial situation, he decided to cancel his holiday plans. Therefore, here 'In light of' would mean 'Because of'.

t: Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted phrase. The speaker addressed the audience with remarkable confidence and clarity.
o: Functioning as a noun
Functioning as an adjective
Functioning as an adverb
Functioning as a subject
e: Answer: C) Functioning as an adverb Explanation: An adverb phrase functions like an adverb and modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. It tells how, when, where, or to what extent something happens. The highlighted phrase: “with remarkable confidence and clarity” modifies the verb “addressed.” addressed how? → with remarkable confidence and clarity Therefore, the phrase functions as an adverb. Why other options are incorrect: A) A noun functions as a subject, object, or complement. The phrase is not naming anything here. B) An adjective modifies a noun/pronoun, but the phrase modifies the verb “addressed.” D) The subject of the sentence is “The speaker,” not the highlighted phrase.

t:
Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence.
Jamie, at the dentist's today, stood up to the <u>baptism of fire</u> pretty well.
o: Lodgings and food
Bad manners
The first experience of something that is usually unpleasant
A man's wife
e:
'Baptism of fire' means learning something the hard way through a challenge or difficulty. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.
The figurative expression for 'lodgings and food' is - Bed and board. 
The figurative expression for 'bad manners' is - Bad form. 
The figurative expression for 'a man's wife' is - His better half.

t:
In the following questions a statement has been given with highlighted text. Select the options that can replace the text with correct idiom or phrase. 
When Chris turned forty, he decided to <u>live his life in excitement</u> and quit his job for his hobbies.
o: Be in the fast lane
Give it a whirl
Snug as a bug in a rug
Palm off
e: IDIOMMEANINGIn the fast laneA life filled with excitement.Give it a whirlTo give something a try.Snug as a bug in a rugWarm and cosy.Palm offPass off something as genuine when it is spurious.So, the correct idiom is 'in the fast lane'. Hence, option (a) is correct.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. 
 Ritu was shocked on learning t hat her kids had ______ somewhere after school
o: wandered off
jumped at
wondered at
finished off
e:
A) Wandered off'का use होगा क्योंकि "wander off" का अर्थ होता है बिना किसी निश्चित दिशा के घूमना या भटकना। Sentence में mention किया गया है कि Ritu को यह जानकर झटका लगा कि उसके बच्चे स्कूल के बाद कहीं भटक गए थे, इसलिए 'wandered off' यहाँ सही है। 'Jumped at' का अर्थ है किसी अवसर पर तुरंत प्रतिक्रिया देना, 'Wondered at' का अर्थ है किसी चीज पर आश्चर्य व्यक्त करना, और 'Finished off' का अर्थ है किसी काम को पूरा करना, जो इस context में सही नहीं है 
 'Wandered off' should be used because it means to move away from a place without a specific direction in mind. The sentence reveals Ritu was shocked upon learning that her kids had gone off somewhere after school, making 'wandered off' fitting here. 'Jumped at' implies eagerly taking up an opportunity, 'Wondered at' means to express surprise at something, and 'Finished off' means to complete something, none of which fit in this context

t: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'Newton's work in the field of physics speaks volumes about his genius.'
o: makes a lot of noise
gives many books
does not give a detailed report
conveys a great deal
e: 'Speaks volumes' means to convey a great deal of information or to make something very clear, even without words (e.g. Her silence spoke volumes about her disappointment). It is used when something communicates a lot through implication, evidence, or inherent quality. 'Makes a lot of noise' and 'gives many books' are literal misinterpretations. 'Does not give a detailed report' is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning. Idiom Tip: When an idiom contains 'speaks' or 'says,' it often relates to communication in a non-literal sense.

t:
Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the give sentence. 
 Shelley has been contemplating for a few days but still has not decided to quit the job.​
o: biting the dust
chewing the cud
cooling one’s heels
getting into hot waters
e:
B)Chewing the cud(idiom) – contemplating or thinking deeply over something गहरे विचार करना 
 Bite the dust(phrase) –fail or come to an end. असफल होना 
 Cool one’s heels(phrase) – be kept waiting. प्रतीक्षा करना 
 Get into hot waters(phrase) – to be in danger, get troubled खतरे में होना

t:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
I had heard of <u>henpecked husbands</u> and now, I felt that I saw one.
o: Controlling husband
Bossy husbands
Oppressed husband
Dominating husbands
e:
• "Henpecked husband" refers to a man who is constantly dominated or controlled by his wife.
• The best match is "oppressed husband," as it implies a husband who is controlled or subdued.
Other options:
• (1) Controlling husband → Incorrect, as "henpecked" means the opposite.
• (2) Bossy husbands → Incorrect, as the wife is usually the bossy one in this context.
• (4) Dominating husbands → Incorrect, as a "henpecked husband" is submissive, not dominant.

t:
Select the idiom that can substitute the underlined group of words. 
After years of hard work, she <u>finally achieved her goal</u>.
o: Crossed the bridge.
Hit the sack.
Saw eye to eye.
Hit the jackpot.
e:
Crossed the bridge: This means to deal with a problem when it arises. 
Hit the sack: This means to go to bed or go to sleep. 
Saw eye to eye: This means to agree with someone. 
Hit the jackpot: This means to achieve great success or get exactly what you want, often unexpectedly or after hard work. 
Given this analysis, the idiom "hit the jackpot" is the most suitable substitute for the underlined group of words, as it accurately describes achieving a goal after years of hard work. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

t: Identify the type of the highlighted phrase. The manager appreciated the employees with exceptional communication skills.
o: Noun Phrase
Adjective Phrase
Adverb Phrase
Gerund Phrase
e: Answer: B) Adjective Phrase Explanation: An adjective phrase is a group of words that functions like an adjective and modifies a noun or pronoun. The highlighted phrase: “with exceptional communication skills” describes the noun “employees.” Which employees? → employees with exceptional communication skills Therefore, it functions as an adjective phrase. Why other options are incorrect: A) A noun phrase functions as a noun, not as a modifier. C) An adverb phrase modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. D) A gerund phrase begins with a gerund (-ing form acting as a noun).

t:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank. 
The government kept the operation _____ to avoid alerting the suspects.
o: Under wraps
On the booze
Break bread
Rolling in the aisles
e: The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'under wraps'. The idiom "under wraps" means to keep something secret or confidential. In the given sentence, it describes the government's action of keeping the operation hidden from public knowledge to avoid alerting the suspects. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence. Option (b) is incorrect. "On the booze" means to be drinking alcohol. Option (c) is incorrect. "Break bread" means to share a meal. Option (d) is incorrect. "Rolling in the aisles" means to laugh uncontrollably. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. The complete sentence is: The government kept the operation under wraps to avoid alerting the suspects.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. 
 ____________, French was the most difficult language for Shruti.
o: Be in the air
Break into
Bear out
By far
e:
D)'By far'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि यह पूरे संदर्भ में सबसे उपयुक्त idiom है। यहाँ वाक्य में Shruti के लिए फ्रेंच भाषा की कठिनाई का उल्लेख हो रहा है और 'by far' idiom उस कठिनाई के स्तर को स्पष्ट रूप से व्यक्त करता है। इसलिए, "By far" सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प होगा। 
 By far'should be used because in the entire context, it is the most appropriate idiom. Here, the sentence is mentioning the difficulty level of the French language for Shruti, and the idiom 'by far' clearly expresses that level of difficulty. Thus, "by far" would be the most appropriate choice.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Rani has ___ about the sanitation in the colony. She can't stop thinking about it.
o: a bird's eye view
a bone to pick
a bee in your bonnet
a bed of thorns
e: "Have a bee in your bonnet" (किसी विषय को लेकर बहुत व्यस्त रहना) refers to a situation where a person feels very strongly about a subject and keeps thinking or talking about it. "A bone to pick" means wanting to discuss an annoyance; "a bird's eye view" means a view from above; "a bed of thorns" means a difficult situation — none match continuous preoccupation.

t: Identify whether the highlighted group of words is a phrase or a clause. The manager postponed the meeting because several important documents were still missing.
o: Noun Phrase
Prepositional Phrase
Clause
Verb Phrase
e: Answer: C) Clause Explanation: A clause is a group of words that contain both a subject and a verb. A phrase does not contain a complete subject-verb combination. In the highlighted part: “several important documents” = subject, “were” = verb Since the group contains both a subject and a verb, it is a clause.

t: Identify whether the highlighted group of words is a phrase or a clause. The athlete entered the stadium with extraordinary confidence and determination despite the pressure of the final match.
o: Clause
Phrase
Noun Clause
Adverb Clause
e: Answer: B) Phrase Explanation: A phrase is a group of words without a complete subject-verb combination. The highlighted words: “with extraordinary confidence and determination” do not contain any subject or verb. Therefore, the group is a phrase.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given group of words: 'A time when money might unexpectedly be needed'
o: A rainy day
A raw deal
A rash of something
A rap over the knuckles
e: 'A rainy day' refers to a time in the future when something (especially money) might unexpectedly be needed - the correct answer. 'A raw deal' means being treated unfairly. 'A rash of something' means a large number of unpleasant events of the same type happening within a short period. 'A rap over the knuckles' means a mild reprimand or scolding. Origin: The 'rainy day' idiom draws on the idea of a literal rainy day when you cannot go out or work, hence needing resources saved up - representing financial prudence.

t: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute italicised words in the given sentence We applaud the family's decision to remain silent over the issue.
o: give a shot
chase rainbows
break the ice
hold their peace
e: Option (d) is the correct answer. The idiom 'hold one's peace' means 'remain silent about something'. The meanings of the Other idioms are- Give a shot- to try to do something. Chase rainbows- trying to do or achieve something that is not really possible or realistic. Break the ice- to start a conversation.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.
After reflecting on the matter regarding his boss's selfish attitude, Raju decided to <u>force himself to perform an unpleasant action in a difficult situation to resolve the matter.</u>
o: Bite the bullet
Dodge the bullet
Shoot the bullet
Ignore the bullet
e:
• Bite the bullet means to endure a painful or unpleasant situation bravely.
• Dodge the bullet means to escape a difficult situation.
• Shoot the bullet and Ignore the bullet are incorrect idiomatic usages.

t:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank. 
You can argue with him _______, but he won't change his mind.
o: Till the cows come home
Head and shoulders above
Standing in good stead
Under the weather
e: The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'till the cows come home'. The idiom "till the cows come home" means for a very long time or indefinitely. In the given sentence, it describes the persistence of arguing with someone who won't change his mind. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence. Option (b) is incorrect. "Head and shoulders above" means significantly better or superior. Option (c) is incorrect. "Standing in good stead" means being in a favourable position or having advantages. Option (d) is incorrect. "Under the weather" means feeling unwell or sick. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. The complete sentence is: You can argue with him till the cows come home, but he won't change his mind.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to fill in the blank in the given sentence. 
 Sweety has been _____________ since her painting won first prize.
o: walking on eggshells
waiting in the wings
walking into the lion's den
walking on air
e: D)walking on air'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि संदर्भ यह है कि Sweety ने अपनी पेंटिंग से पहला पुरस्कार जीता है। इस जीत के कारण वह बहुत खुश हो सकती है, और यहाँ "walking on air" का तात्पर्य बहुत खुश और उत्तेजित होने से है। बाकी के विकल्प संदर्भ से मेल नहीं खाते हैं, इसलिए "walking on air" सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प होगा।

t: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence. Everything in the mansion was in great confusion after the robbery.
o: Pick holes
Pell-mell
Turn over a new leaf
Damp squib
e: "Pell-mell" (अव्यवस्थित ढंग से) means in a confused, rushed, or disorderly manner, perfectly matching a state of disarray after a robbery. "Pick holes" means to criticize; "Turn over a new leaf" means to start fresh; "Damp squib" means something less impressive than expected — none describe disorder.

t: Select the correct meaning of the idiom in bold and italics. The more famous and successful you become, the more money you make. It's a snowball effect.
o: Tendency to become arrogant or selfish.
Increase in amount or degree of something at a fast rate.
The desire to become successful and famous.
Decrease in net worth and popularity.
e:
Snowball effect: a situation in which something grows bigger or more important at an ever-increasing rate; amplify.
Among the options, 'increase in amount or degree of something at a fast rate' is the correct option that matches the meaning of the given idiom. 
Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. 
 My car _______ on the way to college yesterday.
o: broke out
broke down
broke in
broke up
e:
B)Broke down– (phrasal verb) If a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working. खराब हो जाना 
 Broke out– (phrasal verb) To begin suddenly or forcefully, especially referring to something unpleasant like war or disease. फूट पड़ना 
 Broke in– (phrasal verb) To enter a place illegally or forcefully. जबरदस्ती घुसना 
 Broke up– (phrasal verb) To end a relationship, meeting, or gathering. टूट जाना

t:
Select the most appropriate idiom ( in the context) to fill in the sentence. 
 Rohit was ______ when he took important decisions without consulting the family
o: cutting the red tape
told to get a new lease of life
in the same boat
told to fight his own battles himself
e: D) told to fight his own battles himself'इस sentence के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त होगा, क्योंकि इसका अर्थ होता है की किसी को उसकी खुद की समस्याओं का सामना खुद करना पड़ेगा। जब Rohit ने परिवार से सलाह लिए बिना महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए, तो यह माना जा सकता है कि उसे अपनी लड़ाई खुद लड़नी पड़ेगी।

t: Which of the following idioms means 'to be extremely busy or overwhelmed with work or tasks'?
o: Have too many irons in the fire
Keep one's head above water
Twiddle one's thumbs
Have an axe to grind
e:
a) Have too many irons in the fire - To be involved in too many activities or projects at the same time, making it difficult to manage them all effectively.
b) Keep one's head above water - To manage to survive, especially financially, despite difficulties.
c) Twiddle one's thumbs - To do nothing or to be bored because one has nothing to do.
d) Have an axe to grind - To have a private or selfish reason for doing or being involved in something.
Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank. 
The mayor has ___________ from the teacher's union.
o: struck while the iron was hot
gained ground
shot in the dark
rolled up the sleeves
